title: Inside hedge funds' AI agents: Citadel, Bridgewater and Man Group
dek: How Citadel, Bridgewater and Man Group are using AI agents in investment research.
evidence: Oct 27 executive interviews plus earlier first-party technical disclosures; no independent comparison of fund alpha or security outcomes
takeaway: The real test is whether agents improve research quality without displacing independent judgment or acquiring trading authority.

sections.title: Context

bullets.detail: Investment research combines evidence gathering, hypothesis testing and judgment. Agents can accelerate the first two without being trusted to make the final investment decision.

paragraphs: The distinction: Investment research combines evidence gathering, hypothesis testing and judgment. Agents can accelerate the first two without being trusted to make the final investment decision.

sections.title: What's new

bullets.detail: Some analysts use agent counterparts to independently research and challenge theses. Its Second Brain prototype updates research notes from filings, earnings calls and meetings.
Pocket Analyst connects an LLM to specialized investment knowledge, internal data, tools and analyst feedback. AIA Labs is expanding those methods while evaluating agent autonomy.
Alpha Assistant orchestrates code search, signal construction and backtests under researcher-approved plans; leadership warns against accepting polished AI conclusions uncritically.

paragraphs: Citadel: Some analysts use agent counterparts to independently research and challenge theses. Its Second Brain prototype updates research notes from filings, earnings calls and meetings.

sections.title: Evidence & limitations

bullets.detail: Bridgewater reports 84.7% accuracy for a specialized Qwen3 derivative versus a 78.2% frontier baseline across six document-filtering tasks, at 13.8× lower inference cost per task. These are firm-reported results, not investment returns.
The firms describe workflows and selected prototypes, but provide no comparable public measurements of research productivity, autonomous-action failures or incremental trading alpha.

sections.title: Why it matters

bullets.detail: Read-only retrieval and sandboxed backtests are fundamentally different from portfolio changes or order placement. Enforce that boundary through tools, identities and approvals.
Record analysts' assumptions before exposing them to AI recommendations, then check whether they challenge the model's method and contradictory evidence.

bullets.lead: More research isn't necessarily more alpha
bullets.detail: Automated hypothesis generation increases false-discovery risk. Require out-of-sample testing, multiple-testing controls, transaction costs and capacity constraints.

variants.label: Unbounded

variants.label: Bounded
variants.code:
Goal: Challenge an analyst's thesis.
Tools: Read-only sources + sandboxed backtests.
Output: Counterevidence + sensitivities.
Decision: Analyst; no trading permissions.
